chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Jess Stacy's comeback: Carnegie Hall and the New Yorker profile
summary: At Freeman's 50th anniversary concert Stacy returned, the New Yorker ran a profile, and Stacy said he now felt he was doing something worthwhile.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Now, most interesting thing, I don't want to dismiss talking about Jess, but as you know, I did not see, over a period of years, I did not see too much of him and didn't have a chance to work with him. But this is the thing that happened, George Wein gave me a 50th anniversary concert, I think you were there, or I think Stanley was there, at Carnegie Hall about four years ago, and Jess came from the Coast and played on the show.
Did the interview with Whitney Balliot.
Yes, while he was there, we made an album for O'Neal, for Hank O'Neal and Whitney Balliot came down to the record session to interview Jess and that became --
Yes, it was in a profile in the New Yorker. Yes, well, on the strength of that, Jess was now an idol again after all these years and I wrote a

little piece because Jess and I had a wonderful talk, he brought a tape recorder and we had a wonderful discussion about the days, and I told Jess -- Jess said to me, 'You know, for the first time in our life now that I have become a free soloist,' he said, 'I feel that I am doing something worthwhile.'

And I said, 'Jess, you always were doing something worthwhile, but you have now become your own man. You're Jess Stacy and the whole world knows who you are and why do they know who you are, because of your unique style.'

So now after the profile broke in the New Yorker, Jess had become an idol and I have heard, since I have not seen him, since I have been over here, that he has had to turn down the work, there were so many offers. He and his wife had been very happy together and living a quiet life and he wonders if he wants to get back into the rat race of the music business.
So I just don't know whether he's taking all of the work or not.
Say that again, will you, Bud, because it's so nice to think of that happening right now.
